# Purpose and scope

This Pre-Characterization Process Risk Assessment (**RA-001**) prioritizes the A-Mab
drug-substance process parameters for characterization and assigns each parameter a study
type, **before** the characterization studies are executed. It is the first (pre-hoc) risk
assessment of the A-Mab lifecycle of iterative risk assessments: it uses prior knowledge and
early development experience — not the results of the characterization studies — to decide
which parameters carry a credible risk to a critical quality attribute (CQA) and therefore
warrant a multivariate designed experiment, which warrant a univariate study, and which
require only routine control. Its output is the **characterization scope** that is handed to
each per-unit-operation Process Characterization Plan (**PCP-003 … PCP-010**).

**Scope.** The `{python} n_params` process parameters of the drug-substance train (production
bioreactor through final UF/DF), assessed for their prospective (pre-characterization) risk of
impacting the `{python} n_cqa` drug-substance CQAs and for the resulting study-type
assignment. This assessment does **not** classify parameters as CPP/WC-CPP/KPP/GPP — that is
an output of the characterization studies, reported in each PCR and consolidated in the
Process Characterization Master Report (**PCMR-001**); nor does it use the
post-characterization residual risk.

**Basis.** The assessment is derived from the Process Transfer Plan (**PTP-001**) product and
process description and follows the A-Mab quality-risk-management methodology [@amab2009] —
the two-axis CQA criticality tools and the risk-ranking-and-filtering (RRF) study-type rule —
within the ICH Q9 quality-risk-management framework [@ichq9] and the QbD approach of ICH Q8
and Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq11]. The curated per-parameter failure-mode and effect content is the
same content source used to build the post-characterization process FMEA.

# Risk-assessment methodology

## Two distinct criticality assessments

Consistent with the A-Mab case study, two distinct assessments are kept separate [@amab2009].
The **CQA criticality** (quality-attribute criticality) is scored on two axes only —
Tool #1: Risk Score = Impact × Uncertainty, and Tool #2: Severity × Likelihood — explicitly
excluding manufacturing capability and detectability; this yields a continuum of criticality,
not a binary critical / non-critical split. The **process-parameter risk** (this assessment)
then asks, for each parameter, whether its variability could impact a CQA and how the
parameter should therefore be studied. Criticality is treated as a continuum throughout
(ICH Q9) [@ichq9].

## Pre-characterization risk ranking and study-type assignment

Because the characterization studies have not yet been executed, this assessment uses the
**initial** (pre-characterization) risk: a parameter with a credible impact to a CQA has an
uncertain effect and poor in-process detectability (the effect is often detectable only at a
downstream step or at release), so its initial risk is high and it is prioritized for study.
A risk-ranking-and-filtering (RRF) screen scores each parameter's potential main-effect and
interaction impact and assigns the study type accordingly: a parameter with a credible
main-effect and interaction risk to a CQA is carried into the unit operation's **multivariate
designed experiment (DoE)**; a parameter with a credible CQA impact but no expected
interaction is studied by a **justified univariate** study; and a parameter with no credible
CQA impact — one that affects only process performance — is studied **univariately** for its
performance effect [@amab2009]. The classification of each parameter (CPP / WC-CPP / KPP /
GPP) is deliberately **not** assigned here; it is an output of the executed studies.

## Prospective severity and initial risk

The prospective severity of each parameter is taken as the maximum severity of the CQA(s) it
could impact, on the A-Mab severity scale (2–10). The initial risk priority number (RPN =
Severity × Occurrence × Detection) uses the pre-characterization occurrence and detection: an
uncertain effect (higher occurrence) and poor pre-characterization detectability (highest for
viral-clearance attributes, which cannot be detected by in-process testing). The initial RPN
is used only to rank and prioritize; it is expected to fall after characterization and the
resulting control strategy, as shown in the post-characterization process FMEA.

# CQA criticality framework

The CQAs in scope and their criticality (Tool #1 = Impact × Uncertainty; Tool #2 severity) are
given in @tbl-cqa. Attributes rated High (H) or Very High (VH) are treated as *Critical*, and
their associated parameters carry the highest prospective severity.

```{python}
#| output: asis
d = cqa_reg.copy()
d["Acceptance"] = d.apply(lambda r: f"{r.acc_low:g}–{r.acc_high:g} {r.unit}", axis=1)
d = d.rename(columns={"cqa": "CQA", "category": "Category", "criticality": "Criticality",
                      "tool1_score": "Tool #1", "tool2_severity": "Tool #2 sev."})
show(d[["CQA", "Category", "Acceptance", "Criticality", "Tool #1", "Tool #2 sev."]])
```

: Drug-substance CQA criticality framework (Tool #1 = Impact × Uncertainty; Tool #2 = severity). {#tbl-cqa}

# Process-parameter risk ranking and study-type assignment

The prospective risk ranking of every process parameter, with the CQA(s) at risk, the
prospective severity, the initial (pre-characterization) RPN, the assigned study type and the
characterization priority, is given in @tbl-rank. Parameters that could impact a CQA are
prioritized for study; parameters that affect only process performance are ranked Low
(product-quality) priority and studied univariately for their performance effect. The
prospective failure mode and effect underlying each ranking are tabulated in Appendix A.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RA.ra_scope_df())
```

: Pre-characterization process-parameter risk ranking and study-type assignment (initial RPN = prospective Severity × pre-characterization Occurrence × Detection). {#tbl-rank}

Of the `{python} n_params` parameters, `{python} n_quality` carry a credible prospective risk
to a CQA and `{python} n_perf` affect only process performance. `{python} n_high` are ranked
**High** priority (a CQA of severity ≥ 8 at risk), `{python} n_med` **Medium**, and
`{python} n_low` **Low**.

# Characterization scope

The study-type assignment defines the characterization scope handed to the per-unit-operation
plans (@tbl-scope): `{python} n_mv` parameters are assigned to a **multivariate DoE**,
`{python} n_ju` to a **justified univariate** study, and `{python} n_uni` to **univariate**
ranging. Multivariate designed experiments are therefore planned for `{python} n_doe_steps`
unit operations (Steps `{python} doe_steps`); the remaining steps — harvest / clarification
and final UF/DF — carry no credible CQA risk and are characterized univariately.

```{python}
#| output: asis
scope = pd.DataFrame([
    ["Multivariate DoE", n_mv, "Credible main-effect and interaction risk to a CQA"],
    ["Univariate (justified)", n_ju, "Credible CQA risk without an expected interaction"],
    ["Univariate", n_uni, "No credible CQA risk; process-performance study only"],
], columns=["Assigned study type", "Parameters", "RRF basis"])
show(scope)
```

: Characterization scope handed to the Process Characterization Plans (PCP-003 … PCP-010). {#tbl-scope}

This scope is carried into each Process Characterization Plan, which specifies the exact
designs, ranges and acceptance criteria; the executed studies then classify each parameter and
define the design spaces and control strategy (reported in the PCRs and consolidated in
**PCMR-001** and the post-characterization process FMEA).
